_about: Disease-specific answer choices for the CycleGAN review in review_sheet.py. Drafted by an AI sub-agent (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, role-played as retina specialist + medical CV professor) from the seed-42 contact sheets on 2026-10-27; 'repeats-template' (all) and 'bright-block-under-hole' (MH) added by Claude Opus 5.5 after a spot-check. AI-assisted, not a clinical assessment. 'real n' = n-th real training scan in data/gan/real/<class>, sorted by file name; '#n' = sample n of the seed-42 draw.

real_features: A dark pocket separates the layered retinal roof from a brighter lower boundary in most scans; it ranges from a shallow slit (real 19, 24) to a broad, tall space (real 5, 6).
The roof generally remains a connected stack of curved grey and bright bands above the pocket.
Pockets can be central or asymmetric; overall scan curvature varies markedly.
Pocket edges are not always smooth: real 11 and 16 have small projections, and real 27 has a divided-looking pocket.
The bright lower boundary generally continues beneath the pocket, with variable mottled texture below it.

choices.label: Grid, stripes or noise
choices.how_to_spot: Compare retinal tissue with the real strip and before image for a newly imposed regular grid or stripes, rather than ordinary grain or inherited vertical shadows.

choices.label: Blurry retinal lines
choices.how_to_spot: Compare the roof bands with similarly soft real scans and the before image, rejecting only smearing that prevents the bands or pocket boundary being followed.

choices.label: Extra retinal stack
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the real strip for an additional disconnected stack of retinal bands above the main retina, and check the before image to see whether it was introduced.

choices.label: Broken pocket roof
choices.how_to_spot: Compare the connected roofs in the real strip with an abrupt tear through the generated retinal roof, rather than a small irregularity along its underside.

choices.label: No visible pocket change
choices.how_to_spot: Compare against the before image and shallow-pocket real 19 and 24, using this only if no new pocket or comparable structural change can be found.

choices.label: Repeats a common template
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the other samples on this tab and with the real strip: flag it when the retina has nearly the same shape, tilt and lesion as many other generated images whatever its before scan, and the real scans vary more than that.

choices.label: Pocket beyond real range
choices.how_to_spot: Compare pocket height relative to retinal thickness and pocket width relative to scan width against even real 5 and 6, choosing this only for a clear excess.

choices.label: Implausible pocket shape
choices.how_to_spot: Compare the pocket roof, floor and tapering edges with the entire real strip, allowing the projections and divided appearance already present in real 11, 16 and 27.

choices.label: Plausible pocket and layers
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the real strip for a dark space between a connected layered roof and a continuing bright floor, within the observed range of size and asymmetry.

traps: Do not reject a large or ragged pocket just for being large or ragged: compare with real 5, 6, 11, 16 and 27 before choosing a hard flaw.
A shallow pocket can look nearly unchanged at thumbnail size; real 19 and 24 are subtle, so absence of an obvious large pocket is not enough to reject.

real_features: The real strip shows a central opening in the retinal tissue, with a bright basal line continuing underneath.
The two edges commonly rise and curl inward; opening width and edge height vary.
Small dark cavities occur inside the tissue beside the opening, sometimes in clusters.
Some scans have thin curved lines or small bright suspended pieces above the opening (for example real 2, 5 and 7).
The surrounding retina remains layered; the basal brightness and background grain vary.

choices.label: Grid, stripes or noise
choices.how_to_spot: Compare tissue with the real strip and before image for a newly imposed periodic pattern that is distinct from speckle or the thin curves seen in real scans.

choices.label: Smeared hole edges
choices.how_to_spot: Compare the opening edges with similarly soft real scans, selecting this only when smearing prevents the raised tissue and cavities from being followed.

choices.label: Bright block under hole
choices.how_to_spot: Look under the opening for a uniform bright rectangle with straight vertical edges reaching deep below the floor; a mild brightening under the hole (real 16, 18) is normal.

choices.label: Broken hole floor
choices.how_to_spot: Trace the bright floor beneath the opening against the real strip and flag a sharp break or displaced segment rather than a change in brightness.

choices.label: Closed or missing opening
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the before image and real strip for a persisting bridge of retinal tissue where the real examples show an opening, checking that this is not just a narrow dark gap.

choices.label: Repeats a common template
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the other samples on this tab and with the real strip: flag it when the retina has nearly the same shape, tilt and lesion as many other generated images whatever its before scan, and the real scans vary more than that.

choices.label: Cavities swallow surrounding retina
choices.how_to_spot: Compare the extent of dark spaces beside the opening with the most cavity-rich real scans and flag only extension far into otherwise unsupported tissue.

choices.label: Opening beyond real range
choices.how_to_spot: Compare opening width and raised-edge height relative to retinal thickness with the widest and tallest real examples before calling the hole exaggerated.

choices.label: Plausible opening and edges
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the real strip for an open central gap, raised layered edges with optional small cavities, and a continuing basal line.

traps: A central missing piece of retina and cavities in the raised edges are real-set features, not automatic evidence of broken layers.
Small suspended bright pieces and thin overhead curves occur in the real strip; do not automatically call them floating GAN debris.

real_features: Small dark spaces occur near the central dip or within adjacent retinal tissue.
Some spaces have a thin roof; others are narrow vertical or angular gaps at the dip.
The bright lower bands usually continue underneath the small spaces.
Most scans retain a recognisable shallow central dip without a large raised dome.
The spaces vary considerably: real 2 has adjacent cavities, real 10 and 11 have a conspicuous dark cavity, and real 14 has a thin horizontal space.

choices.label: Grid, stripes or noise
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the real strip and before image for a newly regular grid or repeated bars crossing tissue rather than ordinary speckle.

choices.label: Blurry cavity border
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the softer real scans and flag only smearing that makes the cavity border and adjacent layers unreadable.

choices.label: Broken deep bands
choices.how_to_spot: Compare the bright bands beneath the cavity with the real strip and before image, flagging an abrupt displaced or duplicated segment rather than local dimming.

choices.label: No visible cavity change
choices.how_to_spot: Compare the before image and the subtler real scans for a new central cavity or focal layer change, using unsure when the difference is too small to resolve.

choices.label: Repeats a common template
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the other samples on this tab and with the real strip: flag it when the retina has nearly the same shape, tilt and lesion as many other generated images whatever its before scan, and the real scans vary more than that.

choices.label: Oversized or misplaced cavity
choices.how_to_spot: Compare cavity size and position relative to retinal thickness with real 2, 10, 11 and 14, rejecting only a clearly unsupported extension or location.

choices.label: Plausible small central cavity
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the real strip for a small central or near-central dark space with surrounding tissue and continuing bright lower bands.

choices.label: Plausible adjacent cavities
choices.how_to_spot: Compare the adjacent dark spaces with real 2 rather than requiring every image to show one round cavity.

traps: An angular dark cavity or a very thin roof is not automatically an artefact: compare real 10, 11, 14 and 23.
Real 2 already contains multiple adjacent cavities; the repeated generated multi-cavity motif is a diversity concern, not by itself an image-level rejection.

real_features: The retina generally remains a connected band with a shallow or broad central dip.
Several scans have a thin central retinal band and less distinct lower retinal layering than the NORMAL before images.
The bright lower border is variably irregular or mottled rather than uniformly crisp.
Brightness beneath that border varies, including locally bright vertical regions in real 3, 14, 18 and 19.
The real strip includes both sharp scans and soft, low-contrast scans; it does not show the large dark domes seen in the CSC strip.

choices.label: Grid, stripes or noise
choices.how_to_spot: Compare the retinal band with the real strip and before image for newly regular grids or stripes, separating them from irregular bright columns below the retina.

choices.label: Unreadable layer blur
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with soft real 13 and the before image, flagging only loss of readable retinal structure beyond that reference rather than softness alone.

choices.label: Stepped or doubled layers
choices.how_to_spot: Compare the before image and real strip for abrupt stair steps or a second displaced copy of a bright retinal band.

choices.label: No visible tissue change
choices.how_to_spot: Compare lower retinal bands and underlying texture with the before image, using this only if neither changes beyond overall brightness and using unsure for subtle cases.

choices.label: Repeats a common template
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the other samples on this tab and with the real strip: flag it when the retina has nearly the same shape, tilt and lesion as many other generated images whatever its before scan, and the real scans vary more than that.

choices.label: Exaggerated bright column
choices.how_to_spot: Compare any bright column beneath the central retina with real 3, 14, 18 and 19, requiring a clearly more extensive or structure-erasing patch before rejecting it.

choices.label: Unsupported large dark pocket
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the real Stargardt strip for a newly created broad dark separation or open tissue gap absent from these references.

choices.label: Plausible lower-band change
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the real strip for a connected retinal band with subtle lower-band irregularity or altered underlying brightness without an unsupported large cavity.

traps: Bright columns beneath the retina and an irregular lower border already occur in real scans; neither alone establishes an artefact.
A soft, nearly ordinary-looking scan can still resemble this real set (for example real 13); do not equate weak visible disease signal with failed translation.

real_features: The retina is a continuous curved band in most real scans, with a shallow central dip or a flatter profile.
Lower retinal bands vary in definition and thickness; some scans look thin and relatively smooth.
A bright basal band generally continues across the scan, with variable mottled texture below.
Several real scans contain small central dark cavities (real 1, 8, 11 and 12); they are not universal.
The real set spans strongly speckled, soft and clearer scans; real 24 is particularly bright and soft beneath the retina.

choices.label: Grid, stripes or noise
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the real strip and before image for a newly imposed periodic pattern rather than the irregular grain already visible in real scans.

choices.label: Washed-out retinal detail
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with bright soft real 24 and the before image, flagging only washout that makes the retinal bands impossible to follow.

choices.label: Torn central retina
choices.how_to_spot: Compare continuity of the upper retinal surface with the real strip and before image, distinguishing an open surface tear from a dark cavity enclosed in tissue.

choices.label: No visible tissue change
choices.how_to_spot: Compare lower retinal bands and small central spaces with the before image, using unsure if the change could be as subtle as the less distinctive real scans.

choices.label: Repeats a common template
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the other samples on this tab and with the real strip: flag it when the retina has nearly the same shape, tilt and lesion as many other generated images whatever its before scan, and the real scans vary more than that.

choices.label: Oversized central cavities
choices.how_to_spot: Compare the cavity cluster with real 1 before rejecting its size or extent, requiring more than simply the presence of several dark spaces.

choices.label: Unsupported detachment dome
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the real RP strip for a broad dark space lifting the whole retinal band away from its bright base rather than a small space inside the tissue.

choices.label: Plausible continuous retinal band
choices.how_to_spot: Compare with the real strip for a continuous retinal band, variable lower-band definition and a continuing bright base without an unsupported large gap.

choices.label: Plausible small central cavities
choices.how_to_spot: Compare enclosed central dark spaces with real 1, 8 and 11, checking that tissue remains above them and the bright base remains below.

traps: Do not reject all dark cavities: real 1 has a conspicuous cluster, confirmed by opening its individual image.
Brightness beneath the retina and subtle thinning vary in the real set; a bright underside or near-normal-looking profile alone is insufficient for rejection.
